mode.description: Epistemic mode of the operation: does it open new semantic space (divergent), close/refine existing space (convergent), neither (neutral), or context-dependent (mixed)?

branch_effect.description: Effect on ClaimGraph branch topology: does it create new branches, preserve existing ones, merge branches, or terminate a branch? 'unspecified' means the operator does not directly alter branch topology.

operators.name: resolve_conflict
operators.mode_evidence: Creates two new B-prefixed claims representing opposing positions on the contradiction; parent.branch_open=True; parent.status='disputed'. Structural forcing of two distinct semantic directions from a single contradiction point.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:578 — explicitly creates B{n:03d} and B{n+1:03d} claims; sets parent.branch_open=True; these are the canonical 'branches' tracked by T9's recombination trigger.
operators.notes: The only operator that creates B-prefixed claims. B-claims are the unit of branch topology in DES. T9 specifically checks branch_open+all_branches_supported to detect when T1-created branches are ready for synthesis.

operators.name: make_conflict_explicit
operators.mode_evidence: Appends a CONFLICT evidence_ref and sets status='disputed', conflict=False. No new claims generated; no semantic space explored or closed. Pure bookkeeping on existing claim state.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:646 — no new claims created; no claims sealed or merged. Operates entirely within the existing claim's metadata fields.
operators.notes: T2 is a precursor to T1: it marks conflict=False (thus satisfying T1's trigger condition on next cycle if status becomes 'contradicted'). The two-step CRITICAL sequence is T2→T1 when both trigger conditions are met sequentially.

operators.name: request_evidence
operators.mode_evidence: For regular C-claims: adds simulated evidence and may raise confidence — convergent (narrows epistemic uncertainty). For B-prefixed claims: calls evaluate_branch_claim() which forces status='supported', confidence=0.85 — functionally convergent and closure-forcing. However, evidence injection can also raise new questions (divergent side-effect at the loop level). Classified as mixed because the B-claim path has qualitatively different semantics than the C-claim path.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:670 — no new claims created, no claims sealed or merged. For B-claims, status is updated but the branch itself is not terminated (sealed=False).
operators.notes: UNCERTAIN CELL — see uncertain_cells_report.md. The B-claim path of T3 (evaluate_branch_claim fallback: status='supported', confidence=0.85) is functionally a forced convergence that bypasses the normal evidence-weighting pathway. This may be a latent inconsistency: T3 can resolve a branch claim to 'supported' without human-readable evidence reasoning.
operators.implementation_inconsistency: B-claim fallback in evaluate_branch_claim() forces status='supported' and confidence=0.85 regardless of claim content. All branch claims that pass through T3 without an LLM call available will be automatically resolved as supported.

operators.name: decompose_claim
operators.mode_evidence: Creates 2-3 new C-prefixed sub-claims from a single underspecified parent; each sub-claim targets a distinct scope. Structurally expands the semantic surface the DES loop must cover.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:725 — creates new C{n:03d} sub-claims; parent.sealed=True; parent.status='supported'. Creates new active claims for the loop to process.
operators.notes: DOCUMENTED INCONSISTENCY: parent claim is set to sealed=True and status='supported' upon decomposition, despite the trigger being scope=={} (underspecified). Underspecified != supported. This means the parent claim is effectively silenced with a false positive epistemic status. The sub-claims inherit the research obligation, but the parent's status label becomes semantically incorrect.
operators.implementation_inconsistency: Parent sealed as 'supported' on trigger 'underspecified'. These are logically incompatible: a claim is sealed-as-supported when evidence confirms it; sealing an underspecified claim as supported bypasses that requirement.

operators.name: generate_counter_hypothesis
operators.mode_evidence: Generates a counter-claim that contradicts the target claim; sets parent.conflict=True; parent.status='contradicted' or 'disputed'. Opens a new line of epistemic tension. Anti-Delphi mode assigns this to the falsifier role — explicitly adversarial.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:780 — creates one new C-prefixed counter-claim; sets parent.conflict=True. Does NOT create B-prefixed branches directly. However, T5 reliably triggers T1 on the next cycle (by setting status='contradicted'), which does create branches. T5's branch-effect is therefore indirect: it is the upstream cause of branch creation, not the creator itself.
operators.notes: UNCERTAIN CELL for branch_effect — see uncertain_cells_report.md. If we count indirect causation (T5→T1 cascade), T5 is effectively branch_effect=create. If we count only direct ClaimGraph mutations, T5 is branch_effect=unspecified. The results.md trace confirms the T5→T1 cascade empirically (iter 8-9: T5 on C003, iter 9: T1 creates B001/B002).
operators.cascade_evidence: results.md iter 8: T5 fires on C003 (confidence 0.35→0.42, status='contradicted'); iter 9: T1 fires on C003, creates B001/B002.

operators.name: explore_evidence_path
operators.mode_evidence: Appends evidence paths to an existing hypothesis; status→'supported'; confidence→max(0.82, conf+0.15). Moves a hypothesis toward a supported state by grounding it in evidence references. Narrows epistemic uncertainty on a specific claim.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:846 — no new claims created; no claims sealed or merged. Modifies only evidence_refs and confidence of the target claim.
operators.notes: In Anti-Delphi mode, T6 is assigned to the hypothesis_builder role. This is noteworthy: T6 is convergent (evidence-grounding) but assigned to the builder role. The builder role is constrained to conf in [0.41, 0.55], which may suppress the confidence boost T6 normally applies (→0.82).

operators.name: refine_qualifier
operators.mode_evidence: Adds a temporal or geographic qualifier to a scoped claim; confidence+=0.05. Refines the claim's precision rather than expanding its scope. Convergent in the sense of narrowing applicability. However, qualifier addition can be seen as a minor semantic expansion (adding a new dimension), hence medium confidence.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:875 — modifies qualifier field and confidence only. No claims created, sealed, or merged.
operators.notes: UNCERTAIN CELL for mode — see uncertain_cells_report.md. T7's mode classification depends on whether 'adding a qualifier' is interpreted as convergent (scope narrowing: claim now applies to a more specific domain) or mixed (adding a temporal/geographic dimension can expose new questions about the specified period/region). The confidence boost (+0.05) suggests the system treats qualification as a convergent epistemic move.

operators.name: seal_claim
operators.mode_evidence: Irrevocably marks a claim as sealed. No further operations will be applied to it. This is the terminal convergent operation: it closes epistemic processing on a specific claim.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:898 — claim.sealed=True. Sealed claims are excluded from all future transition-table evaluation. The claim's epistemic trajectory is terminated.
operators.notes: T8 also functions as an explicit fallback (des.py:1020): if no other transition fires and a supported+high-confidence claim exists, T8 seals it. This means T8 has dual roles: primary seal trigger and loop-progression fallback. The fallback use is important for loop termination dynamics.

operators.name: trigger_reframing
operators.trigger: branch_open == True AND all branches status == 'supported'
operators.mode_evidence: Creates a synthesis claim (is_synthesis=True, status='supported', conf≥0.82) from two or more branch claims; parent.sealed=True; reframing_count++. The synthesis integrates multiple divergent trajectories into a single supported position — the canonical convergent operation in the DES.
operators.branch_effect_evidence: des.py:926 — creates synthesis claim from branch claims; parent.sealed=True. This is the only operator that explicitly combines multiple branch trajectories into a unified claim. Branch topology collapses from multiple open branches to one synthesis node.
operators.notes: T9 fires when all branches are status=='supported', NOT when all are sealed. The results.md trace confirms: T9 fires on iter 23 when B001 is sealed and B002 is supported-but-not-sealed. T7→T8 on B002 fires AFTER T9. This means the synthesis can precede the formal sealing of its input branches — a potential sequencing inconsistency. Also: is_synthesis claims bypass T3-T7 evaluation (des.py synthesis_bypass check), which prevents synthesis claims from being decomposed or counter-hypothesized. The reframing_count>2 hard limit (des.py) means at most 3 T9 firings per session.

empty_cells.note: No operator; preservation achieved passively by NOT firing T9
No operator; divergent claims can only be terminated via convergent path (T6→T8)
No operator; convergent operations do not open new semantic space
